
## Rezafungin · a once-weekly echinocandin

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
**Mechanism and chemistry**

- Structural analogue of **anidulafungin** sharing its lipid side chain. The C5 ornithine **hemiaminal** is
  replaced by a **choline aminal ether**, which blocks the non-enzymatic ring-opening that degrades
  anidulafungin.
- Target and spectrum are unchanged: **β-1,3-D-glucan synthase**, fungicidal against *Candida*.
- The chemistry *is* the pharmacology: greater chemical stability produces a **half-life >130 h** and
  front-loaded exposure.

**Microbiology**

- Spectrum essentially identical to the older echinocandins, including *C. auris* and azole-resistant
  *N. glabratus*; no activity against *Cryptococcus* or Mucorales.
- At vaginal pH 4, MICs (including *C. parapsilosis*) sit below achievable intravaginal concentrations.
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
::: {.caution}
**A methodological caution with real consequences.** EUCAST and CLSI rezafungin MICs diverge notably because
rezafungin **binds non-specifically to plastics** — microtitre plates, pipette tips, reservoirs. Adding
**0.002% Tween 20** to the medium normalises MICs across plate types and laboratories while preserving
wild-type/non-wild-type separation [@hoenigl2024novel].
:::

::: {.pearl}
**Resistance** remains FKS-mediated. *In vitro* the spontaneous mutation frequency conferring reduced
susceptibility is low (1.35 × 10^−8^ to 3.86 × 10^−9^) and ~20 serial passages are needed to select
resistance.
:::
:::
:::

## Rezafungin · pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Half-life | ~**80 h** after the first dose; ~**150 h** after the second or third — linear kinetics |
| C~max~ (single dose) | 19.2 mg/L |
| Steady-state AUC~0–24~ | 827 mg·h/L |
| Protein binding | 97% |
| Metabolism | **Minimal** — most circulating and excreted drug is unchanged |
| Elimination | 75% faeces, 25% urine; plasma clearance 3.1 mL/min |
| Dose adjustment | **None** for renal or hepatic impairment |
| Population PK | Three-compartment model; no covariate (body surface area, albumin, disease state, age, sex, race, creatinine clearance) produced clinically meaningful change — **one regimen for all adults** |

**Regimen:** 400 mg IV in week 1, then **200 mg IV once weekly**.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.keypoint}
**PK/PD rationale.** Front-loaded C~max~/MIC with a very long terminal phase. Population PK/PD modelling
showed rezafungin reached the stasis target for **all** *N. glabratus* isolates from 2018–2020 surveillance,
whereas caspofungin, micafungin and anidulafungin failed to do so at approved doses [@hoenigl2024novel].
:::

::: {.pearl}
**Tissue penetration.** A single rezafungin dose produced higher concentrations in intra-abdominal abscesses
and liver at 48 and 72 h than daily micafungin in a murine model. CSF, vitreous and urinary penetration remain
**low**, as for the class.
:::
:::
:::

## Rezafungin · clinical evidence

| Trial | Design | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **STRIVE** (phase 2) | Rezafungin 400 mg weekly, or 400 mg then 200 mg weekly, vs caspofungin | Day-14 overall cure 60.5% / 76.1% / 67.2%. The **400/200 mg** regimen gave the highest cure and lowest 30-day mortality; candidaemia cleared more rapidly |
| **ReSTORE** (phase 3, NCT03667690) | Double-blind, double-dummy vs caspofungin; 199 adults with candidaemia and/or invasive candidiasis; non-inferiority margin 20% | **Global cure at day 14: 59.1% vs 60.6%**; **30-day all-cause mortality 23.6% vs 21.2%** — non-inferior on both the EMA and FDA primary endpoints [@thompson2023restore] |
| **Pooled STRIVE + ReSTORE** | Mycological response at day 14 by species | *C. albicans* 67% vs 67%; ***N. glabratus* 84% vs 63%** (between-group difference 21.4, 95% CI 1.9–40.8); *C. tropicalis* 74% vs 64%; *C. parapsilosis* 79% vs 70% |
| | Subgroup mortality | Favoured rezafungin in patients **≥65 years** (−17.6%, 95% CI −32.5 to −2.8) and **CrCl <60 mL/min** (−18.2%, −33.1 to −3.2) |
| **ReSPECT** (phase 3, ongoing) | Rezafungin 400/200 mg weekly vs fluconazole or posaconazole plus co-trimoxazole in allogeneic HSCT | First prospective trial of an echinocandin for **prevention of invasive aspergillosis** in this population; endpoint fungal-free survival at day 90 |
| **RADIANT** (phase 2) | Topical gel/ointment for vulvovaginal candidiasis | **Inferior to oral fluconazole** — programme discontinued |

## Rezafungin · safety and place in therapy

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
**Safety**

- In ReSTORE, treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in **91%** of rezafungin and **85%** of caspofungin
  recipients — in a population with high baseline illness: pyrexia 14% vs 5%, hypokalaemia 13% vs 9%,
  pneumonia 10% vs 3%, anaemia 9% in both.
- Grade ≥3 events 49% vs 51%; serious adverse events 55% vs 49%; discontinuation for an adverse event 9% in
  both arms. Treatment-related serious events were rare (one infusion reaction, one urticaria).
- **No QT prolongation** at single doses up to 1400 mg.
- Label precautions: infusion-related reactions, **photosensitivity**, hepatic reactions.
- **No clinically significant drug interactions** across CYP and transporter probe substrates.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.keypoint}
**Where it fits.** Once-weekly IV dosing converts candidaemia from a reason to keep a central line and a
hospital bed into an outpatient-manageable disease. In the ECMM Candida III cohort, **16%** of candidaemia
patients required prolonged hospitalisation and a further **4%** received outpatient parenteral therapy — so
roughly one in five is a candidate on logistics alone.
:::

::: {.caution}
**Unresolved.** Whether prolonged sub-MIC tails in colonising flora select FKS mutants is unknown, as is
whether higher front-loaded exposure helps against isolates that already carry hot-spot mutations. Dose
adjustment was not needed for mycological cure in the small number of resistant isolates in the trials.
:::
:::
:::
